message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Physical State (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 kg m⁻³) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| | Specific heat (gas, 25 °C) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume (ideal gas, 25 °C) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Diffusivity (air) | ~0.61 cm² s⁻¹ |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ (≈0.0016 M) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Bond type | Diatomic (H₂) |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % (v/v) in air |
| | Oxidation state | +1 (in most compounds) |
| | Common oxidation states | +1, –1 (hydride) |
| | Acidic behavior | Acts as a weak acid (H⁺ donor) in aqueous solution |
| | Basic behavior | Forms hydrides (e.g., LiH, CaH₂) which are strong bases |
| | Redox behavior | Reduces many metal oxides; oxidized to water or hydroxide |
| | Hydride formation | Forms ionic hydrides with alkali/alkaline earth metals |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Role in water | Constituent of H₂O; proton (H⁺) in acid-base chemistry |
| | Role in acids | Provides H⁺ in Brønsted–Lowry acids |
| | Role in fuels | Used in fuel cells (electrochemical conversion to electricity) |
| | Role in nuclear fusion | Deuterium–tritium fusion (D + T → He + n + 17.6 MeV) |
| **Miscellaneous** | Spectral lines | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µB (proton magnetic moment) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Stability | Stable protium; deuterium stable; tritium radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y) |

---

### Summary

Hydrogen is the lightest and simplest element, existing as a diatomic gas under normal conditions. Its unique combination of low mass, high diffusivity, and extreme flammability makes it both a useful energy carrier (fuel cells, rocket propellant) and a potential source of clean power via nuclear fusion. Chemically, hydrogen behaves as a versatile participant in acid–base reactions, redox processes, and hydride formation, playing a central role in water chemistry and organic synthesis.
